# Parameteriser

> Parameteriser is a Python package for **kinetic parameter lookup** from the BRENDA enzyme database and sequence databases. It retrieves Km, kcat, Ki and other kinetic parameters for enzymes, supports BLAST-based sequence comparison across organisms, and provides estimation and visualization of parameter distributions. Maintained by the Computational Biology group at RWTH Aachen.

## BRENDA interface

The BRENDA module provides two API versions for querying kinetic parameters:

- **v1** (`parameteriser.brenda._v1.Brenda`) — SOAP-based API. Requires email/password credentials. Queries BRENDA's web service directly.
- **v0** (`parameteriser.brenda.v0.Brenda`) — Selenium-based web scraper. Reads from a local JSON database dump or crawls the BRENDA website. Provides `get_kms()`, `get_kcats()`, `get_kms_and_kcats()`, and `read_database()`.

```python
from parameteriser.brenda.v0 import Brenda

client = Brenda()
kms, kcats = client.get_kms_and_kcats("2.7.11.1")
# kms: DataFrame with columns [value, substrate, organism, uniprot, commentary, is_mutant, is_recombinant]
```

## BLAST sequence search

`blast_sequence_against_others` runs a protein BLAST query against a set of sequences to find homologs across organisms. Requires `blastp` and `makeblastdb` on PATH.

```python
from parameteriser import blast_sequence_against_others

results = blast_sequence_against_others(query_sequence, proteome_sequences)
# DataFrame with columns [qseqid, evalue, pident, qcovs]
```

## Parameter estimation

`estimate_mean_std` estimates mean and standard deviation of a parameter distribution using kernel density estimation.

```python
from parameteriser import estimate_mean_std

mean, std = estimate_mean_std(kms["value"])
```

## Selection and display utilities

- `select_organism(df, organism)` — filter DataFrame rows by organism, drop organism column
- `select_substrate(df, substrate)` — filter DataFrame rows by substrate, drop substrate column
- `print_organisms(df)` — print sorted unique organisms from a parameter DataFrame
- `print_table(vals)` — print a formatted table of strings

## Plotting

- `plot_parameter_distribution(kms, title)` — KDE plot of a single parameter distribution with rug marks
- `plot_parameter_distributions(all_kms, organism_kms, organism_name=...)` — overlaid KDE comparing all organisms vs. a specific one, with boxplots

## Quick start

```python
from parameteriser.brenda.v0 import Brenda
from parameteriser import select_organism, estimate_mean_std, plot_parameter_distribution

client = Brenda()
kms = client.get_kms("2.7.11.1")  # hexokinase

# Filter to a specific organism
human_kms = select_organism(kms, "Homo sapiens")

# Estimate parameters
mean, std = estimate_mean_std(human_kms["value"])

# Plot distribution
plot_parameter_distribution(human_kms["value"], "Hexokinase Km (Homo sapiens)")
```

## Installation

```bash
uv sync              # PyPI; BRENDA interface only
pixi install          # conda-forge; includes deepmolecules (broken)
```

## Notes

- The `deepmolecules` integration (sequence-based parameter prediction) is currently broken due to a numpy 1/2 version mismatch. Only the BRENDA web interface is functional.
- The v0 BRENDA client caches downloaded data locally. Use `read_database()` with a BRENDA JSON dump for offline use.
- BLAST search requires NCBI BLAST+ tools installed separately.

## MCP Server

[MxlMCP](https://computational-biology-aachen.github.io/mxl-mcp/mxlpy/latest) is a Model Context Protocol server for the MxlPy ecosystem. It exposes modeling, simulation, fitting, and analysis capabilities as tools that AI assistants can call programmatically.

## Tool family

Parameteriser is part of a tool family for systems biology:

- [MxlPy](https://github.com/Computational-Biology-Aachen/mxl-python) — mechanistic learning library (Python ODEs + ML)
- [MxlBricks](https://github.com/Computational-Biology-Aachen/mxl-bricks) — composable reaction building blocks
- [MxlModels](https://github.com/Computational-Biology-Aachen/mxl-models) — pre-defined model files (generated from MxlBricks)
- [MxlWeb](https://github.com/Computational-Biology-Aachen/mxl-web) — browser ODE solver (SvelteKit + WebWorkers)
- [PySBML](https://github.com/Computational-Biology-Aachen/pysbml) — SBML import/export bridge
